summary: ARP proxy cache aging on branch AP causes WireGuard peer heartbeat loss and route collapse
description:
Issue summary:
Branch office in SF intermittent connectivity: several employees report corporate resources unreachable while on office Wi‑Fi. Affected hosts maintain WireGuard tunnels to the corporate edge; tunnels show as UP but traffic to internal services fails.

What happened: During periods of high AP client churn (lunch hour), multiple WireGuard peers lose ability to reach internal subnets. The WireGuard status shows handshake/peer alive but route traffic drops and internal DNS stops resolving.

Initial hypothesis: AP-level ARP proxy or switch-level ARP suppression may be expiring entries aggressively; WireGuard peer heartbeat (UDP) uses ephemeral local MAC entries for next-hop to the gateway and when ARP cache ages out, packets are not forwarded correctly causing asymmetric paths.
impact: ~30% of on-site engineers in SF branch experienced inability to reach internal services (git, internal API) for short windows (30s–3m). No customer-facing services impacted. Productivity hit during peak lunch period. Multiple SRE engineers reconnected manually.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Connect a laptop to SF-office Wi‑Fi SSID (corporate-ssid) and establish WireGuard tunnel to corporate-edge (wg0).
2) Produce sustained client churn by toggling Wi‑Fi on/off for 10 clients or run a 100-client simulated association script on AP (lab reproduced the effect),
3) Observe WireGuard peer state: peer shows latest handshake timestamps but traffic to 10.0.0.0/16 stops responding,
4) Capture AP switch MAC/ARP tables during churn, notice target gateway MAC entry removed/aged leading to failure to forward to on-prem route next-hop.
logs: Mar 10 11:57:03 wg0: peer 10.9.254.12 handshake ok latest=11s
Mar 10 11:57:17 kernel: arp_cache: removed entry 10.9.254.1 -> aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff on vlan200
Mar 10 11:57:20 snap-agent[netmon]: tcpdump: no responses from 10.9.240.5:80 after 3 retries
Mar 10 11:57:45 AP-switch: ARP proxy age-threshold triggered for 10.9.254.0/24, flushed entries (config threshold=30s)
investigation_notes: 11:30 - Support triage: Confirmed multiple reports, created aggregated client list and times. No central config changes pushed during window.
11:45 - Packet captures collected on affected client and AP uplink. Observed UDP heartbeats for WireGuard reaching AP but subsequent ARP lookup failing for next-hop IP on VLAN.
12:05 - Repro in lab: running simulated churn led to ARP proxy flush on AP model (Aruba 5400 series) when MAC churn > 60 clients/min. Reproduces route collapse for tunneled clients behind NAT.

12:30 - Cross-check with switch team: STP and port-security not implicated; feature 'ARP proxy caching' and 'gratuitous ARP handling' present and configured with low aging timers on affected AP firmware (v8.2.1).

12:55 - Hypothesis refined: aggressive ARP proxy cache aging on AP causes transient loss of L2 next-hop for the gateway IP used by WireGuard, packets are forwarded to wrong port until ARP entry rebuilt. WireGuard reports handshake timestamps because the kernel sees incoming responses from peer node (asymmetric traffic) but encapsulated payload cannot be delivered through L2 until ARP resolved.
comments: Aisha Khan (2026-03-10 11:38): Initial ticket created after 4 independent Slack reports in #it-support. Included client machine MACs and times.

Marco Rivera (2026-03-10 12:10): Added AP switch logs and initial packet captures. Spun up lab with same AP model and reproduced churn. Suspect AP firmware defaults too aggressive for our WireGuard use-case.

SRE-Oncall (Lina Chen) (2026-03-10 12:40): Noted that dedicated on-prem firewalls do not show drops; downstream NAT is fine. Suggest bumping ARP age to 300s as workaround. Will coordinate with Networking team.

Network Eng (Raj Patel) (2026-03-10 13:05): Confirmed device model and firmware. Raise firmware to v8.2.5 includes ARP proxy fix but flagged release notes. Will schedule config change on SF AP cluster during low-risk window.

Marco Rivera (2026-03-12 09:30): Applied temporary mitigation: increased ARP proxy cache timeout to 300s on AP cluster; monitoring shows no recurrence during lunch hour. Preparing change request for permanent fix and firmware rollout.
Aisha Khan (2026-03-12 10:02): Teams confirmed user impact cleared; marking investigation complete pending rollout.
resolution: Temporary mitigation applied: ARP proxy cache aging timer increased from 30s to 300s on SF AP cluster during maintenance window. Lab reproduction confirmed mitigation prevents WireGuard peer heartbeat loss under churn. Network team to schedule firmware upgrade (v8.2.5+) which contains a targeted ARP proxy stability fix and improved gratuitous ARP handling. Post-deploy: run 1-week observation window and then revert to standard timer if safe. Follow-ups: add monitor on AP ARP flush events to our telemetry, update branch network runbook with recommended ARP cache settings for VPN-heavy environments.
next_steps: 1) Network Eng to schedule firmware upgrade for SF AP cluster to v8.2.5 and roll out to other branches after validation (owner: Raj Patel, ETA 2026-03-20).
2) SRE to add alerting for AP ARP-cache flush events and correlated WireGuard packet loss (owner: Lina Chen, ETA 2026-03-18).
3) Update branch runbook and include recommended ARP cache and gratuitous ARP config for corporate-ssid (owner: Documentation, ETA 2026-03-22).
4) After 1-week observation, decide on permanent ARP timer baseline and close ticket.
